i am working on the branch incident-tracking-latest, relating to the incident dashboard.

i would like to add enhancements to the dashboard itself, namely improved analytics. these are the four that is being considered:

1. Incident Resolution Efficiency (MTTR - Mean Time To Resolve)
What it tracks: Average time taken from when an incident is logged (auto or manual) to when its status is marked as CLEARED or RESOLVED.

Visual: A single KPI card (e.g., "Avg. Resolution Time: 14m") or a weekly trend line comparing response speed.

2. AI Confidence vs. False-Positive Rate Chart
What it tracks: A breakdown of incidents created by AI vs. those marked as FALSE POSITIVE or deleted/cleared.

Visual: A simple donut chart or percentage badge showing "AI Accuracy Rate: 88%" or a scatter/bar plot comparing Confidence Score ranges (e.g., 90–100% vs. 70–89%) against valid vs. false alerts.

3. Source Breakdown (AI-Detected vs. Manually Logged Incidents)
What it tracks: Comparative ratio of automated AI detections vs. manual CCTV logging over time.

Visual: A simple split bar or pie chart showing the percentage of incidents caught by AI (Facial Recognition vs. Object Detection) vs. manually reported by FM staff.

4. Incident Escalation & Resolution Status FunnelWhat it tracks: How incidents move through the lifecycle pipeline (Active > Investigating > Escalated > Cleared).

Visual: A horizontal pipeline/funnel chart or status distribution bar.

---

the specifics are subject to change after further consideration; this is a initial draft. the most important thing is preventing scope conflict. for each of the four suggested visuals, can you search the entire project and ensure there is nothing similar to each of the four?

do not edit anything yet; this request is simply a searching task.

Full CRUD dashboard for security incidents generated by AI (FR = Facial Recognition, OD = Object Detection) or manually by FM staff.

**Files:**
- `client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx` — React component, all CRUD logic
- `client/src/css/IncidentDashboard.css` — all styles (badges, cards, toasts, animations)
- `server/routes/incident.js` — Express routes (POST /, GET /, GET /:id, PATCH /:id, DELETE /:id, POST /scan-frame)
- `server/models/IncidentLog.js` — Sequelize model, `paranoid: true` (soft delete)

**Route guard:** `ACCESS.FM_ONLY` in App.jsx, isFM block in Sidebar.jsx

**Model columns:** camera_location, status (detection type e.g. UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS), person_name, confidence_score, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), source (Facial Recognition/Object Detection/Manual), resolutionStatus (Active/Investigating/Escalated to Security/Cleared), notes

**Seed:** 12 static incidents seeded once on first load, gated by localStorage flag `flowguard_incidents_seeded`. All seed incidents start with resolutionStatus='Active'.

**Filters:** Client-side on the fetched data — search (person+location), severity, source, resolutionStatus.

**Animations:** 
- Row slide-in (`.inc-row-new`): new rows after create
- Row slide-out (`.inc-row-deleting`): 350ms animation, then removed from state
- Toast stack: `.incToastEnter`/`.incToastExit` animations using max-height trick for natural document-flow push

**Toast system:** `toasts` array state, `toastCounterRef` for IDs, 3s timer per toast, types: success (green), delete (red), error (amber). Stacked in document flow between filter bar and table.

**Back-to-top:** Scroll listener on `mainRef.current` (dashboard-main div), not window. Position calculated from getBoundingClientRect for horizontal centering.

**Table truncation:** 30 chars for location + person name, full text in title tooltip and detail modal.

**DEFERRED (not implemented):**
- Live data seeding from AI scan-frame into the dashboard
- No changes to any other page

**How to apply:** Live AI integration route exists (`POST /scan-frame`) but the frontend dashboard doesn't subscribe to it — it only shows manually created + seeded data.

FlowGuard is a security management system for Harrison Food Factory. Three roles: FM (Facility Manager), Staff (Security Staff), Tenant.

**Stack**: React (Vite) frontend + Node.js/Express backend + PostgreSQL via Sequelize. Frontend on `client/`, backend on `server/`.

**Roles + access constants** defined in `client/src/constants/roles.js` — ACCESS.FM_ONLY, ACCESS.FM_STAFF, ACCESS.FM_TENANT.

**Sidebar** (`client/src/components/Sidebar.jsx`) has conditional NavLinks per role. isFM, isStaff, isTenant flags.

**Key pages** (FM-only): User Management `/users`, Security Review `/security-review`, Incident Dashboard `/incidents`, Tenant Onboarding `/tenant-management`, Settings `/settings`.

**CSS pattern**: Each page has its own CSS file. Shared base: `Dashboard.css` (layout), `Management.css` (table, modals), `Users.css` (action buttons). Page-specific file extends these patterns.

**How to apply:** Maintain this pattern when adding new pages — don't create monolithic CSS, extend the shared base.

content.text:
Search complete — no code was touched. Here's what exists today, mapped to your four proposed features:

## 1. MTTR / Resolution Efficiency
**No conflict — clean slate, but a data-modeling gap to flag.** Nothing computes resolution time anywhere in the app. However, `IncidentLog` ([IncidentLog.js](server/models/IncidentLog.js)) has no `resolvedAt`/`clearedAt` timestamp — only Sequelize's default `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. `updatedAt` isn't a safe proxy since any PATCH (notes, severity, person_name) bumps it, not just a move to Cleared. Precedent elsewhere in the codebase: `SupportTicket` ([SupportTicket.js:46](server/models/SupportTicket.js#L46)) has a dedicated `resolvedAt` column that's set only on resolution — worth mirroring that pattern on `IncidentLog` if you want accurate MTTR math. (SupportDashboard doesn't actually use that field for any metric yet either, so there's no chart to collide with there.)

## 2. AI Confidence vs. False-Positive Rate
**No conflict on data/route level, but a naming collision risk.** `FacialEvaluation.jsx` already has an "Accuracy" stat card (`stats.accuracy`, [FacialEvaluation.jsx:517](client/src/pages/FacialEvaluation.jsx#L517)) plus False Accept/Reject Rate — but it's computed from evaluator-confirmed ground-truth samples in a completely separate evaluation harness, unrelated table, unrelated page. If your new widget is also called "AI Accuracy Rate," it'll read as the same metric to anyone who's seen both pages — recommend a distinguishing label (e.g. "Incident Confidence Accuracy"). Separately: `IncidentLog.resolutionStatus` has no `False Positive` value (`ALLOWED_STATUSES` = Active/Investigating/Escalated to Security/Cleared in [incident.js:14](server/routes/incident.js#L14)) — false positives today are handled by hard-deleting the row (soft-delete via `paranoid: true`), not by tagging it. You'd need to either count soft-deleted rows or add a real status/flag to get a false-positive rate.

## 3. Source Breakdown (AI vs. Manual)
**Direct overlap — this already exists in simplified form.** [IncidentDashboard.jsx:422-427](client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx#L422-L427) already renders an `.inc-source-counter` bar: "AI Detected: X | Manually Logged: Y", driven by `sourceCounts` ([IncidentDashboard.jsx:261-264](client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx#L261-L264)) which buckets `source !== 'Manual'` vs `source === 'Manual'`. This is exactly the ratio your feature wants — just as text chips instead of a chart. Building a new, separate chart alongside it would be redundant; this reads as an upgrade target (replace the chip row with the donut/split-bar) rather than a net-new feature.

## 4. Escalation & Resolution Status Funnel
**Partial overlap, worth reconciling rather than ignoring.** [IncidentDashboard.jsx:402-420](client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx#L402-L420) already has a 4-card `.inc-stats-grid`: Total, Critical, Investigating, Cleared. But it's not a clean status funnel — "Critical" mixes severity + Active status, and "Investigating" merges two distinct resolutionStatus values (`Investigating` + `Escalated to Security`) into one bucket ([IncidentDashboard.jsx:266-271](client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx#L266-L271)). A true 4-stage funnel (Active → Investigating → Escalated to Security → Cleared) would need to either replace this stat grid or sit alongside it without duplicating the same numbers in two visual forms. Also note: `SecurityReview.jsx` has its own unrelated status lifecycle (`Pending Review`, `False Positive`, `Escalated`, `Resolved`, [SecurityReview.jsx:10](client/src/pages/SecurityReview.jsx#L10)) — different feature, different table, no charts there currently, but the shared word "Escalated" is a terminology collision to keep straight in labeling, not a code conflict.

## Broader context worth knowing

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\gladw\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\bundled-skills\2.1.220\a96164d4d4790dcf1462dd803ac80010\dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values — touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe — run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure — do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job — magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). → `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) — each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. → `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette — run the script, don't reason about ΔE.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,…>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory — or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, ≥8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. → `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer — by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. → `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For ≥ 2 series a legend is always present and ≤ 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box — the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** — its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout — open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** — it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue — it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale → two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake — see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light→dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD ΔE ≥ 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6–8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL — full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead — see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view — it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for ≥ 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** — values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance — every value filled in — is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical — steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of — build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong — check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** — every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

13	| A single ratio against a limit | **Meter** (same-ramp track) | A pie of 2 slices |

21	|---|---|---|

23	| Trend over time | line; area for a single series | sequential or 1 categorical |
24	| Tell distinct series apart | grouped/stacked bar, multi-line | **categorical** |
25	| One series is the point, rest are context | **emphasis** (highlight one, gray the rest) | 1 hue + gray |
26	| Above/below a baseline; Δ to target | diverging bar, or line vs baseline | diverging |
27	| Part-to-whole | **stacked bar** (go horizontal for many / long-named categories) | categorical |
28	| Ordered-scale share (Likert, sentiment, agree↔disagree) | **diverging stacked bar**, centered on neutral | diverging |

48	|---|---|

# Choosing a form

Decide this **before** color. The data's job picks the form — and sometimes the
right form is not a chart.

## Is it even a chart?

| The data is… | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| A single current value (+ maybe a trend) | **Stat tile** (value + delta + sparkline) | A one-bar bar chart |
| A handful of headline numbers | **KPI row** of stat tiles | A grouped bar chart |
| The one number a dashboard leads with | **Hero figure** (≥48px, sans) | — |
| A single ratio against a limit | **Meter** (same-ramp track) | A pie of 2 slices |
| More than ~7 classes that all carry meaning | A **table** (or table + chart) | More colors |

If a chart *is* right, pick the type by the job:

## The job → the type

| Job (what the reader must do) | Default form | Color job |
|---|---|---|
| Compare magnitude, low → high | bar / column; **heatmap** for a grid | sequential (one hue) |
| Trend over time | line; area for a single series | sequential or 1 categorical |
| Tell distinct series apart | grouped/stacked bar, multi-line | **categorical** |
| One series is the point, rest are context | **emphasis** (highlight one, gray the rest) | 1 hue + gray |
| Above/below a baseline; Δ to target | diverging bar, or line vs baseline | diverging |
| Part-to-whole | **stacked bar** (go horizontal for many / long-named categories) | categorical |
| Ordered-scale share (Likert, sentiment, agree↔disagree) | **diverging stacked bar**, centered on neutral | diverging |
| Before → after per item | dumbbell | 1 hue, 2 shades |

## The rules behind the table

- **Sequential is the safe default.** One hue, more-is-darker. It stays legible and
  consistent and is hard to misread. Reach for it unless the data's job is
  specifically *identity* or *polarity*.
- **Categorical is for when the series ARE the subject** — and it has a real cost:
  it can bury the one data point that actually matters. If the story is "this one
  went up," that's **emphasis**, not categorical.
- **Emphasis** = the most underused form. One series in the accent hue, the rest in
  the de-emphasis gray. Often the honest answer to "make this chart clearer."
- **Texture is an opt-in expression, not a default form.** It earns its place only
  for accessibility (full CVD), print/export, and `forced-colors`. Never decorative.
  → see `marks-and-anatomy.md`.

## Series-count ladder (categorical)

| Series | Treatment |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | color alone is comfortable for everyone; direct-label |
| 4 | adjacent forms (stacks, bars, lines) stay gate-safe, but direct labels become mandatory — yellow and orange now share the screen; all-pairs forms (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small multiples) cap at **three** — fold to "Other" or facet rather than seat a 4th |
| 5–6 | soft cap; legend or small multiples |
| 7–8 | token ceiling; past it, fold the tail into "Other," facet into small multiples, or use composite encoding (hue × shape) |

Never solve "too many series" by generating more hues. A generated 9th hue is
indistinguishable from an existing one under CVD and breaks every check.

1	# Color formula
2	
3	Color is **not hand-picked**. Every chart color does exactly one of four jobs, and a
4	palette is legal only if it passes six checks. The checks are the product — they are
5	what makes a palette safe to change and what lets the same method run on any design
6	system's ramps.
7	
8	## The four jobs
9	
10	| Job | What it encodes | Structure |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| **Categorical** | identity (which series) | 8 hues, fixed order, assigned in sequence, never cycled |
13	| **Ordinal** | position in a sequence (funnel stage, tier, bucket) | one hue, monotone lightness steps; light end still ≥ 2:1 on surface |
14	| **Sequential** | magnitude (how much) | one hue, steps 100→700, light→dark; flips anchor in dark |
15	| **Diverging** | polarity (which side of a baseline) | two hues + a neutral gray midpoint; equal steps per arm |
16	| **Status** | state (good→critical) | a small fixed scale, reserved meaning, always icon+label |
17	
18	**Categorical or ordinal?** If swapping the category order would change the
19	meaning — funnel stages, size tiers (S/M/L), age bands, cohort buckets — it is
20	**ordinal** and takes a one-hue ramp so the reader sees the order in the color.
21	If swapping would not — product names, teams, regions, endpoints — it is
22	**nominal categorical** and each bar takes the *same* slot-1 hue (one series,
23	so no legend box — the title names it), or slots 1..N when there are N separate
24	series. Never color nominal bars by their value: that spends the identity channel
25	re-encoding what bar length already shows.
26	
27	## The six checks
28	
29	Every categorical color — current or proposed — must pass all six.
30	
31	1. **Fixed hue anchors.** Eight families in a fixed order. The order is the
32	   CVD-safety mechanism; it never changes. *(structural — enforced, not measured)*
33	2. **Lightness band per mode.** OKLCH L ≈ 0.43–0.77 light; ≈ 0.48–0.67 dark. *(validator)*
34	3. **Chroma floor.** OKLCH C ≥ ~0.10 — below it a hue reads as gray and stops doing
35	   identity work. *(validator)*
36	4. **CVD separation.** ΔE here and everywhere in this method is Euclidean distance
37	   in OKLab ×100. Target ≥ 8 / floor ≥ 6 (floor legal only with secondary encoding),
38	   under protanopia & deuteranopia simulated with Machado–Oliveira–Fernandes 2009 at
39	   severity 1.0 — the thresholds are calibrated to that simulation model, so the
40	   model is part of the standard, not an implementation detail. A companion
41	   **normal-vision floor** gates the same pairs under unsimulated vision: worst
42	   pair ΔE ≥ 15, so neighbors stay easy to tell apart for full-color readers too.
43	   This floor is a hard gate — secondary encoding does not excuse it.
44	   (This floor is what forced the first of the July 2026 re-orders of the
45	   documented default palette — same hues and steps, re-ordered; the current
46	   default clears it at 19.6 light / 19.3 dark; see `palette.md`.)
47	   *Adjacent* pairs for
48	   stacks/bars/lines (only neighbors touch — assignment never skips); **all pairs for
49	   scatter, bubble, choropleth, and small-multiples**, where any two marks can sit side
50	   by side — pass `--pairs all` there or a real collapse stays hidden. All-pairs is
51	   a strictly harder test, and it caps how many series those chart forms can carry:
52	   the documented default validates all-pairs with its **first three slots** in both
53	   modes, and no ordering of the full eight can pass (the all-pairs pairlist doesn't
54	   depend on order). More than three series in an all-pairs form means fewer series
55	   (fold to "Other") or facets — not a palette change. *(validator)*
56	5. **Contrast vs surface.** ≥ 3:1 for marks; conditionally relaxed where values are
57	   readable another way (visible labels or the table view). *(validator)*
58	6. **Documented palette only.** Every slot is a hex from the instance file
59	   (`palette.md` or its equivalent) — no eyeballed values. *(structural; for a
60	   customer's ramps, snap to nearest — below)*
61	
62	## Run the checks — never eyeball them
63	
64	```
65	node scripts/validate_palette.js \
66	  "#2a78d6,#eb6834,#1baf7a,#eda100,#e87ba4,#008300,#4a3aa7,#e34948" --mode light
67	```
68	
69	(`scripts/` is relative to this skill's base directory, shown at the top of the prompt.)
70	
71	(or load it as `<script type="module">` in the chart's own page — it reads
72	`data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report)
73	
74	Reports each computable check (2–5) with PASS / WARN / FAIL plus the worst CVD pair.
75	Exit 0 = no hard FAIL (WARN bands — floor-band CVD 6–8 and sub-3:1 contrast
76	relief — still exit 0 and require secondary encoding); exit 1 on any FAIL,
77	including a normal-vision floor below 15, which is a hard gate. Run once per mode
78	(`--mode dark --surface "#1a1a19"`), and add
79	`--pairs all` for scatter / bubble / map / small-multiples charts (where any two marks
80	can be neighbors — the default adjacent check would hide a collapse). For an
81	**ordinal** ramp pass `--ordinal` — it switches to the ramp checks (monotone L,
82	adjacent ΔL ≥ 0.06, light-end contrast ≥ 2.0:1, single hue) instead of the
83	categorical six.
84	A WARN on CVD (6–8 floor) is legal **only** if you also ship secondary encoding
85	(direct labels, gaps, or texture). A FAIL on the normal-vision floor says
86	full-color readers will struggle to tell the flagged neighbors apart.
87	On the *adjacent* pairlist, re-step one of the pair; secondary encoding does
88	not excuse this one. On `--pairs all`, a floor FAIL over many series is the
89	series cap binding (check 4): cut the series count, facet, or switch chart
90	form — re-ordering or re-stepping cannot make eight colors pairwise-distinct
91	at this floor. A WARN on contrast is **not dismissable** — it
92	obligates a relief channel (visible direct labels or the table view); shipping the
93	sub-3:1 fill with neither is a fail.
94	
95	**Scope — what the validator does and doesn't cover.** These six checks validate a
96	*categorical* palette (series identity). They do **not** judge a lone status/text
97	color or a sequential ramp. For a single status or text color, run a WCAG *text*-
98	contrast check (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) — `validate_palette.js` exports
99	`contrast(a, b)` for exactly this. For sequential/diverging, the check is lightness
100	monotonicity across the ramp, not adjacency CVD — running the categorical validator on
101	a sequential ramp **will FAIL by design** (it spans the band; steps sit close), which
102	is expected, not a real failure; don't "fix" a good ramp to satisfy it.
103	
104	## Snap-to-passing (any design system)
105	
106	Given a customer's ramps and a desired order:
107	1. For each slot, pick the step whose OKLCH L sits in the mode's band and C ≥ floor.
108	2. Run the validator. For any adjacent pair below the ΔE 8 target, nudge one slot
109	   ± a step (hold its hue, move its lightness) and re-run.
110	3. Repeat until the worst adjacent pair clears the floor. Function preserved, the
111	   customer's hues kept.
112	
113	## Themes
114	
115	The slot **order** is a separable, named choice — a *theme* — on the same hues and
116	the same six checks. Each design system names a default order and any alternates;
117	swapping themes tunes the mood without touching the method. A surface adopts one
118	theme and freezes it; never mix themes within a dashboard. (See `palette.md`.)
119	
120	**Deriving an order when a system has no theme yet:** don't guess. Enumerate candidate
121	orderings of the system's hues, run the validator on each, and pick the one that
122	maximizes the *minimum adjacent* CVD ΔE. (Seeding from a known-good order by hue-family
123	analogy, then optimizing, is fine — the default in `palette.md` came out of
124	exactly that enumeration, as one of the tied top orders under the gates,
125	picked among them for its opening.)
126	
127	## Status is fixed
128	
129	Status never follows the theme — it is a small fixed scale (good → warning → serious
130	→ critical) with reserved meaning, on steps deliberately distinct from the categorical
131	slots so a status color never impersonates a series, and always paired with an
132	icon + label (on a light surface warning and serious sit below 3:1 by design —
133	the pairing is the mitigation). (Exact steps in `palette.md`.) The collision rule: when a series *means* good/bad (error rate, pass/fail) it wears
134	status tokens; when it's just "series 4" it wears categorical — never both in one chart.
135

The slot **order** is a separable, named choice — a *theme* — on the same hues and
the same six checks. Each design system names a default order and any alternates;
swapping themes tunes the mood without touching the method. A surface adopts one
theme and freezes it; never mix themes within a dashboard. (See `palette.md`.)

**Deriving an order when a system has no theme yet:** don't guess. Enumerate candidate
orderings of the system's hues, run the validator on each, and pick the one that
maximizes the *minimum adjacent* CVD ΔE. (Seeding from a known-good order by hue-family
analogy, then optimizing, is fine — the default in `palette.md` came out of
exactly that enumeration, as one of the tied top orders under the gates,
picked among them for its opening.)

## Status is fixed

Status never follows the theme — it is a small fixed scale (good → warning → serious
→ critical) with reserved meaning, on steps deliberately distinct from the categorical
slots so a status color never impersonates a series, and always paired with an
icon + label (on a light surface warning and serious sit below 3:1 by design —
the pairing is the mitigation). (Exact steps in `palette.md`.) The collision rule: when a series *means* good/bad (error rate, pass/fail) it wears

36	one swatch restates the title and costs space.

1	# Reference palette
2	
3	This is the **reference instance** of the data-viz method: every parameter the
4	method needs, filled in with a validated default palette. The rest of the skill
5	is system-agnostic — **to target your brand, substitute this file's values** and
6	re-run the validator. Nothing else changes.
7	
8	## How to use these values
9	
10	Everything below is plain hex. In an HTML chart, **define the slots you use as
11	CSS custom properties in a local `<style>` block** at the top of the file, then
12	reference them by role throughout — so the light/dark values swap in one place,
13	and the chart body is written against roles rather than raw hex:
14	
15	```css
16	.viz-root {
17	  color-scheme: light;
18	  --surface-1:      #fcfcfb;   /* chart surface */
19	  --text-primary:   #0b0b0b;
20	  --text-secondary: #52514e;
21	  --series-1:       #2a78d6;   /* categorical slot 1 */
22	  /* …only the roles this chart uses */
23	}
24	@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
25	  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
26	    color-scheme: dark;
27	    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
28	    --text-primary:   #ffffff;
29	    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
30	    --series-1:       #3987e5;
31	  }
32	}
33	:root[data-theme="dark"] .viz-root {
34	  color-scheme: dark;
35	  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
36	  --text-primary:   #ffffff;
37	  --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
38	  --series-1:       #3987e5;
39	}
40	```
41	
42	Declare the dark values under both scopes as above — the media query covers
43	the OS setting; the `data-theme` scope covers the viewer's theme toggle,
44	which must win both ways (the `:not(…)` guard lets a light stamp beat
45	OS-dark; `:where()` keeps the media block below the toggle scope).
46	
47	## Categorical palette
48	
49	Both modes are selected. The dark column is the same eight hues stepped for the
50	dark surface, not a separate palette:
51	
52	| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark |
53	|------|-----|-------|------|
54	| 1 | blue | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
55	| 2 | orange | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
56	| 3 | aqua | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
57	| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
58	| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
59	| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
60	| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
61	| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |
62	
63	This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
64	pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD ΔE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
65	(OKLab ×100, ≥8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision ΔE 19.6 light / 19.3
66	dark (≥15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
67	multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors — with all 28 pairs in
68	play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
69	re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule — so those
70	chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
71	in both modes** (worst pair CVD ΔE 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
72	light / 20.9 dark — clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
73	facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
74	together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
75	light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
76	sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
77	visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
78	dark band (OKLCH L ≈ 0.48–0.67, ≥ 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
79	set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening —
80	the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
81	changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
82	dark run in the 6–8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
83	this order deliberately trades that fourth slot — yellow now sits beside orange —
84	for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow↔orange
85	confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
86	pure re-order.) When you swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full
87	gate.
88	
89	The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic — candidate
90	orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
91	modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
92	passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
93	your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
94	choose only among the passing ones.
95	
96	## Sequential hue
97	
98	Default single hue: **blue**, light→dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
99	once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
100	one-hue ramp.
101	
102	| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
103	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
104	| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
105	| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
106	| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
107	| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |
108	
109	The full 100→700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude —
110	heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
111	to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks —
112	funnel stages, tiers — validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
113	must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
114	2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).
115	
116	## Diverging pair
117	
118	**blue ↔ red** — warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray
119	(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue↔aqua was
120	rejected — both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as "nothing".)
121	
122	## Status palette (fixed — never themed)
123	
124	| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |
125	|---|---|---|---|
126	| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |
127	| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |
128	| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |
129	| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |
130	
131	Dark: same four steps — all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain
132	distinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and
133	serious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so
134	a status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct
135	from the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series —
136	distinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to
137	carry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar
138	(unsimulated ΔE ≥ 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit
139	below 15 — in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure
140	4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text
141	green `#006300` sits 10.1 from the series green; green vs status-good (9.7)
142	holds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. The rule is general: any series color beside a
143	same-hue-family status or delta cue leans on the icon + label pairing and on
144	placement; never on hue alone.
145	
146	## Texture fill (the accessibility channel)
147	
148	One hand-drawn **"Lines"** fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror only**. Inked
149	tone-on-tone (a darker step of the fill's own ramp). On value scales it is
150	*ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging sign).
151	Triggered by the accessibility setting, print, or `forced-colors` — never
152	decorative, never on by default.
153	
154	## Surfaces (for the validator)
155	
156	- Light chart surface: `#fcfcfb`
157	- Dark chart surface: `#1a1a19`
158	
159	These are the validator's built-in defaults. **When you swap in your own
160	palette, re-run against your own surfaces:**
161	`--surface <your-light> --mode light` and `--surface <your-dark> --mode dark` —
162	contrast and band results are only meaningful against the surface the chart
163	actually renders on.
164	
165	## Chart chrome & ink
166	
167	| Role | Light | Dark |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
170	| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
171	| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#ffffff` |
172	| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
173	| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
174	| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
175	| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
176	| Delta ↑ good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
177	| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |
178	
179	## Filter controls
180	
181	Filters are standard UI, not chart components — the chart layer only adds the
182	composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
183	rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
184	bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
185	footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.
186	
187	## Typeface & figures
188	
189	Everything — including the hero figure — stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
190	-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
191	standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
192	figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
193	vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.

| 4 | yellow | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
| 5 | magenta | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
| 6 | green | `#008300` | `#008300` |
| 7 | violet | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
| 8 | red | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |

This order passes every hard gate in both modes on the default *adjacent*
pairlist (stacks, bars, lines): worst adjacent CVD ΔE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark
(OKLab ×100, ≥8 target), worst adjacent normal-vision ΔE 19.6 light / 19.3
dark (≥15 floor). Under `--pairs all` (scatter, bubble, choropleth, small
multiples) the full eight cannot clear the floors — with all 28 pairs in
play no ordering can (the pairlist no longer depends on order), and
re-stepping is off the table by the documented-palette rule — so those
chart forms carry a series cap: **the first three slots validate all-pairs
in both modes** (worst pair CVD ΔE 9.2 light / 9.4 dark, normal-vision 24.0
light / 20.9 dark — clear of the CVD warn band). Past three, fold to "Other" or
facet: the fourth slot puts yellow and orange on screen
together, and that pair fails the all-pairs floors (normal-vision 13.7
light; CVD 4.8 dark). Three light-mode slots (magenta, yellow, aqua)
sit below 3:1 contrast on the light surface: the **relief rule** applies (ship
visible direct labels or the table view). The dark steps were chosen for the
dark band (OKLCH L ≈ 0.48–0.67, ≥ 3:1 on the dark surface) and validated as a
set. (Ordering history: adopted July 2026 for its more harmonious opening —
the same eight hues and steps as its predecessor, re-ordered, zero hex
changes. The predecessor validated its first FOUR slots all-pairs, with its
dark run in the 6–8 CVD warn band, so secondary encoding was required there;
this order deliberately trades that fourth slot — yellow now sits beside orange —
for better-looking leading colors. Revisit the trade if yellow↔orange
confusion shows up in real charts with four or more series; undoing it is a
pure re-order.) When you swap in your own ramps, hold your palette to the full
gate.

The slot **ordering** is the CVD-safety mechanism, not cosmetic — candidate
orderings were enumerated and only those clearing every adjacent gate in both
modes kept (see `color-formula.md` § Themes); this default is one of the
passing orders, picked among them for its opening colors. When you swap in
your brand's hues, do the same: run the validator on candidate orderings and
choose only among the passing ones.

## Sequential hue

Default single hue: **blue**, light→dark. When two sequential contexts appear at
once, the second takes the next categorical slot's hue (orange), each as its own
one-hue ramp.

| step | hex | step | hex | step | hex | step | hex |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | `#cde2fb` | 250 | `#86b6ef` | 400 | `#3987e5` | 550 | `#1c5cab` |
| 150 | `#b7d3f6` | 300 | `#6da7ec` | 450 | `#2a78d6` | 600 | `#184f95` |
| 200 | `#9ec5f4` | 350 | `#5598e7` | 500 | `#256abf` | 650 | `#104281` |
| | | | | | | 700 | `#0d366b` |

The full 100→700 range is for **sequential** encoding (continuous magnitude —
heatmaps, choropleths) where the lightest step means "near zero" and is allowed
to recede toward the surface. For an **ordinal** ramp (discrete ordered marks —
funnel stages, tiers — validated with `--ordinal`), the step nearest the surface
must still clear 2:1: on light, start no lighter than **step 250** (`#86b6ef`,
2.06:1); on dark, go no darker than **step 600** (`#184f95`, 2.15:1).

## Diverging pair

**blue ↔ red** — warm/cool poles that read as opposite. Neutral midpoint is gray
(light `#f0efec`, dark `#383835`). Equal step count per arm. (blue↔aqua was
rejected — both cool, the midpoint doesn't read as "nothing".)

## Status palette (fixed — never themed)

| role | hex | light-surface contrast | dark-surface contrast |
|---|---|---|---|
| good | `#0ca30c` | 3.27 | 5.19 |
| warning | `#fab219` | 1.79 | 9.49 |
| serious | `#ec835a` | 2.57 | 6.60 |
| critical | `#d03b3b` | 4.68 | 3.62 |

Dark: same four steps — all clear 3:1 on the dark surface (`#1a1a19`) and remain
distinct from the dark categorical slots. On the light surface, warning and
serious are sub-3:1 by design; the **icon + label** pairing is the mitigation, so
a status color never carries meaning alone. These steps are deliberately distinct
from the categorical slots so a status color never impersonates a series —
distinct enough that nothing collides at a glance, not enough for hue to
carry the distinction unaided: measured by the series floor's own bar
(unsimulated ΔE ≥ 15), around nine categorical-vs-status pairs per mode sit
below 15 — in light mode red vs critical and yellow vs warning both measure
4.8, slot-2 orange sits 5.8 from status-serious, and the light success text
green `#006300` sits 10.1 from the series green; green vs status-good (9.7)
holds in both modes, since both hexes are mode-invariant. The rule is general: any series color beside a
same-hue-family status or delta cue leans on the icon + label pairing and on
placement; never on hue alone.

## Texture fill (the accessibility channel)

One hand-drawn **"Lines"** fill, used at **45° and its 135° mirror only**. Inked
tone-on-tone (a darker step of the fill's own ramp). On value scales it is
*ordered* (rotation steps with magnitude; arm angle carries the diverging sign).
Triggered by the accessibility setting, print, or `forced-colors` — never
decorative, never on by default.

## Surfaces (for the validator)

- Light chart surface: `#fcfcfb`
- Dark chart surface: `#1a1a19`

These are the validator's built-in defaults. **When you swap in your own
palette, re-run against your own surfaces:**
`--surface <your-light> --mode light` and `--surface <your-dark> --mode dark` —
contrast and band results are only meaningful against the surface the chart
actually renders on.

## Chart chrome & ink

| Role | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| Chart surface | `#fcfcfb` | `#1a1a19` |
| Page plane | `#f9f9f7` | `#0d0d0d` |
| Primary ink | `#0b0b0b` | `#ffffff` |
| Secondary ink | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
| Muted (axis/labels) | `#898781` | `#898781` |
| Gridline (hairline) | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
| Baseline / axis | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
| Delta ↑ good (success text) | `#006300` | `#0ca30c` |
| Border (hairline ring) | `rgba(11,11,11,0.10)` | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` |

## Filter controls

Filters are standard UI, not chart components — the chart layer only adds the
composition rules in `interaction.md`. A date-range control is a list of preset
rows (today, last 7/30/90 days, month-to-date) with selection marked by a 16px
bold check, hover as a ghost wash, and custom range behind a hairline in the
footer. Dimension filters are a standard combobox.

## Typeface & figures

Everything — including the hero figure — stays in the system sans: `system-ui,
-apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`. No display or serif face anywhere. Large
standalone numbers (hero figure, stat-tile values) use the default proportional
figures; reserve `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns that must align
vertically (table rows, axis ticks). Substitute your brand's UI sans here.

# Interaction — tooltips & filters

An HTML chart is interactive by default — the hover layer is part of the deliverable,
not an upgrade. Omitting it is the exception (a bare stat tile), never the default.
Design it with the same care as the static render.

## Tooltips & hover

Tooltips **enhance, they never gate**: every value a tooltip shows is also reachable
without it, through direct labels or the table view. Same details on keyboard focus
as on hover.

- **The crosshair finds the X.** A vertical hairline tracks the pointer and snaps to
  the nearest data position. Readers aim at a date, never at a 2px line.
- **On bars and cells, the mark is the hit target.** No crosshair — each bar, segment,
  dot, or heat-cell carries its own `pointermove`/`focus` tooltip showing category and
  value, and the hovered mark lifts (slight lighten or outline) so the reader sees it respond.
- **One tooltip, every series.** The readout lists every series at that X — the
  pointer never has to land on a line or a fill to get a value.
- **Labels are untrusted data — use `textContent`.** Series and category names
  often come from CSV headers, tool output, or API responses. Insert them into
  tooltip/legend/table DOM with `textContent` or `createTextNode`, never via
  `innerHTML` string concatenation.
- **Values lead, labels follow.** In the tooltip the value is the Strong,
  high-contrast element and the series name is secondary — the legend's hierarchy
  inverted, because here the reader has the series and wants the number.
- **Line keys, not boxes.** Tooltip rows key their series with a short stroke of the
  series color; at tooltip density a filled box is data-weight ink doing a label's
  job. (Legends still mirror the mark: rect for bars/areas, line for lines.)
- **The hit target is bigger than the mark.** A mark's hover/focus area includes its
  2px surface gap and then some — never only the painted pixels. An 8px scatter dot is a
  pinpoint nobody hits reliably; give each point a transparent hit area of at least
  **24px**, or — for dense scatter — a nearest-point / Voronoi layer so the pointer only
  has to be *closest*, not dead-center. (The crosshair already does this for the X on
  line and bar charts; scatter and bubble need the per-point version.)
- **A value pushed off its mark lives in the tooltip.** When a label won't fit inside a
  small bar (see `marks-and-anatomy.md`), that bar's hit area carries the value on hover
  and focus — the tooltip is its overflow home, and the table view keeps it reachable
  without hovering at all.

## Filters & time ranges

Every monitoring dashboard needs the same controls. These are **standard UI, not
chart marks** — build them with ordinary HTML form controls styled to match the
chart chrome. Dataviz only adds composition rules:

- **One row, above the charts.** Filters sit in a single left-aligned row above the
  content they scope — never inside a chart card, never per-chart. If one chart needs
  its own range, it's a different dashboard.
- **Date range first.** It's the filter every reader reaches for; presets (today,
  last 7 / 30 / 90 days) before a custom range.
- **Filters scope everything below them.** Every chart, stat, and table re-renders
  against the same slice, so the numbers always agree.
- **Refetch keeps the frame.** While data reloads, charts hold their previous render
  at reduced opacity — no skeleton, no layout jump, no flash.

A good date picker lists presets as rows (nobody fights a calendar grid for "last 30
days"), marks selection with a 16px bold check, keeps hover a ghost wash so it never
competes with selection, and tucks the custom range behind a hairline in the footer.
(See `palette.md` for the reference spec.)

# Server migrations

Plain, idempotent SQL migrations for the live PostgreSQL database. The project has
no Sequelize-CLI migration framework, so these are hand-run `.sql` files. Every file
is written to be safe to run more than once (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, no drops).

## Running a migration

From the `server/` directory, using the same credentials as `.env`
(`DB_HOST` / `DB_PORT` / `DB_USER` / `DB_NAME`):

```bash
# PowerShell / Windows (psql from the PostgreSQL install)
$env:PGPASSWORD = "<DB_PWD>"
& "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin\psql.exe" `
    -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres -d flowguard `
    -f migrations/20260714_sync_object_detection_schema.sql
```

input.content:
# Incident Dashboard — Deep Analytics Enhancements

## Context

The Incident Dashboard (`client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx`) currently ships CRUD + a coarse 4-card stat grid + a plain-text "AI Detected: X | Manually Logged: Y" counter. A prior search pass (this session) confirmed none of the four proposed analytics existed anywhere else in the app, but found two spots that were direct upgrade targets rather than net-new: the source counter (already showing the right ratio, just as text) and the stat grid (already showing status-ish counts, but not a clean lifecycle funnel).

Decisions locked in with the user this session:
- Keep the main dashboard **focused on immediate action items only** — the existing 4-card stat grid (Total/Critical/Investigating/Cleared) is **not touched**.
- The text source-counter **is replaced** with a compact horizontal split-bar + circular-dot legend, on the main dashboard.
- A **new "Deep Analytics" subpage**, reachable only via a "View Deep Analytics →" button on the Incident Dashboard (no sidebar entry — mirrors the existing hidden-page precedent at `/logistics/gate-verification`), holds the two genuinely new, heavier analytics: MTTR (item 1) and AI Confidence vs. False-Positive Rate (item 2), plus the Escalation & Resolution Funnel (item 4), which was originally a stat-grid "upgrade" candidate but is being built fresh on the subpage instead so the main dashboard stays uncluttered.
- **A new `'False Positive'` resolutionStatus value is added** (plain string column, no migration needed for this part) so AI incidents can be explicitly marked false-positive instead of only ever being hard-deleted — this is what item 2's accuracy metric is computed from.

All chart forms and colors below were chosen using the project's `dataviz` skill and validated against this app's actual dark surface (`#1e2539`) with `scripts/validate_palette.js` — not eyeballed. Two notable findings from that validation, both worth remembering during review: (a) the app's **existing** source-badge colors (`#38bdf8`/`#c084fc`/`#94a3b8`) and status-badge colors (`#f59e0b`/`#fbbf24` in particular) fail the colorblind-safety checks already, today, in shipped code — out of scope to fix here; (b) the **new** components below intentionally use a different, validated hue set, which is a deliberate trade-off (documented inline) not an inconsistency to "fix."

---

## 1. Backend changes

### 1.1 Model — `server/models/IncidentLog.js`
Add a nullable `resolvedAt` field (`DataTypes.DATE`, `allowNull: true`), next to `resolutionStatus`.

### 1.2 Migration — new `server/migrations/20260803_add_incident_resolved_at.sql`
Follow the existing idempotent style (`server/migrations/20260729_sync_missing_columns.sql` is the template): header comment explaining purpose/safety, then
```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE incident_logs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "resolvedAt" TIMESTAMPTZ;
COMMIT;
```
No backfill — existing Cleared incidents get `resolvedAt = NULL` and simply don't contribute to MTTR until they're touched again. (`updatedAt` was considered and rejected as a backfill proxy: it's bumped by unrelated edits like notes changes, so it would misreport resolution time.) Add a row to `server/migrations/README.md`'s table.

### 1.3 Route — `server/routes/incident.js`
- `ALLOWED_STATUSES` (line 14): append `'False Positive'`.
- `RESOLUTION_TO_ALERT_STATUS` (lines 19-24): **leave unchanged, deliberately**. `DetectionAlert`'s own `VALID_STATUSES` (in `detectionAlerts.js`) has no false-positive analog, so a PATCH that sets `resolutionStatus: 'False Positive'` simply won't touch the linked alert's status — already the route's existing safe no-op path for any unmapped value.
- PATCH `/:id` (lines 210-250): add resolvedAt stamping.
  - Define `const TERMINAL_STATUSES = ['Cleared', 'False Positive'];`
  - When `resolutionStatus` is present in the request: if it's entering a terminal state and `resolvedAt` isn't already set, stamp `resolvedAt = new Date()`. If it's **leaving** a terminal state back to Active/Investigating/Escalated (a reopen) and `resolvedAt` was set, clear it back to `null`. Otherwise leave `resolvedAt` untouched.
  - Reasoning for the clear-on-reopen behavior: MTTR should reflect the incident's *current* resolution cycle, not a stale timestamp from a first resolution that got reopened.

### 1.4 No new backend aggregation endpoint (explicit decision)
`GET /api/incident` already returns every field every chart needs (`source`, `confidence_score`, `resolutionStatus`, `createdAt`, and after 1.1/1.2, `resolvedAt`) for every incident. Compute all four analytics client-side (Section 3.4) rather than adding a `server/services/incidentAnalytics.js` + route — this matches how `stats`/`sourceCounts` are already computed client-side on this exact page today, keeps the subpage's numbers trivially in agreement with the main dashboard (same source list, no separate query to drift), and is easiest to iterate on for an "initial draft." Revisit server-side aggregation (mirroring `server/services/dashboardAnalytics.js`'s pattern) only if `GET /` ever gains pagination or the incident list grows large enough that shipping full rows becomes wasteful.

---

## 2. Main dashboard: source split-bar (replaces the text counter)

File: `client/src/pages/IncidentDashboard.jsx` + `client/src/css/IncidentDashboard.css`

### 2.1 Data
Replace the `sourceCounts` memo (currently `{ai, manual}` at lines 261-264) with a 3-way bucket:
```js
const sourceCounts = useMemo(() => {
  const manual = incidents.filter(i => i.source === 'Manual').length;
  const fr     = incidents.filter(i => i.source === 'Facial Recognition').length;
  const od     = incidents.length - manual - fr; // everything else — see note below
  return { manual, fr, od };
}, [incidents]);
```
**Important correction found during planning**: `IncidentLog.source` isn't limited to the 3 literal values — `detectionAlerts.js` and `edgeDetectionAlerts.js` also write `'Browser Webcam'`, `'Uploaded Video'`, and `'SecurePi Edge Node'` into real `IncidentLog` rows. The existing badge helper `sourceClass()` (lines 33-39) already handles this correctly via a default-else branch that buckets anything non-Manual/non-FR as "Object Det." — the `od = total - manual - fr` computation above mirrors that exactly, so the 3 segments always sum to the full incident count and always agree with the table's existing OD badges. Do **not** write `i.source === 'Object Detection'` for the third bucket — it would silently under-count.

### 2.2 Component
Single horizontal bar, 3 segments (Manual / Facial Recognition / Object Detection), replacing the `.inc-source-counter` chips block:
- `role="img"` + `aria-label` summarizing all 3 counts, plus a visually-hidden `sr-only` table mirroring exact values — same accessible-chart convention as `AlertTrendChart.jsx`/`TopAlertZonesChart.jsx`.
- Bar: ~12px thick (well under the 24px mark-spec cap, reads as "compact" per the ask), 4px rounded ends on the two outer edges only, a 2px surface-color gap between segments (background gap, not a border — no stroke).
- Each segment is hoverable/focusable (`tabIndex`, `title`) showing its category + count.
- Legend below the bar: one row per segment, a **circular** dot (distinct from the existing square `.legend-swatch` used elsewhere) + label + count — e.g. "● Manual (4)". Counts are inline in the legend text itself, not hidden behind hover, so every value is reachable without a pointer.
- Guard divide-by-zero when there are no incidents (empty-state track, all counts 0).

### 2.3 Colors — validated
```
Facial Recognition → #3987e5 (blue)
Object Detection   → #d95926 (orange)
Manual             → #199e70 (aqua/teal)
```
Ran through `validate_palette.js` as a categorical, all-pairs, dark-mode palette against this app's `#1e2539` card surface — **all checks pass** (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD separation ΔE 9.4 deutan / normal-vision ΔE 20.9, contrast ≥3:1). By contrast, the existing table badge triplet (`#38bdf8`/`#c084fc`/`#94a3b8`) **fails** CVD separation between FR/OD under protanopia (ΔE 1.9) — a real, pre-existing issue, not something newly introduced. **Trade-off to flag in the PR**: the new bar's legend colors will visibly differ from the existing table's source badges for the same 3 categories, on the same page. Call this out explicitly in the PR description so it reads as an intentional accessibility fix, not an inconsistency bug. (Reconciling the table badges to match is a separate, larger follow-up — it'd touch `ObjectDetection.jsx` too — out of scope here.)

### 2.4 "View Deep Analytics →" button
Add next to the existing "Support Tickets →" button inside `.inc-header-actions` (around line 396-398), same `useNavigate` pattern already in use:
```jsx
<button className="inc-analytics-btn" onClick={() => navigate('/incidents/analytics')}>
  View Deep Analytics →
</button>
```
Give it its own distinct accent (e.g. teal/cyan gradient) so it doesn't read as "the same feature" as the Support Tickets button.

### 2.5 'False Positive' status wiring (rides along with this file's other edits)
- `statusClass()` (lines 23-31): add a case for `'False Positive'` → a new neutral/slate badge class (reuse the same slate tone as the Manual source badge — "not a real threat" reads as neutral, not one of the four existing active/investigating/escalated/cleared hues).
- Add `'False Positive'` as an option to both the filter-bar status `<select>` (~lines 464-475) and the edit-modal status `<select>` (~lines 684-694) — these are currently two independent hardcoded copies.
- **Worth doing while touching both**: extract the resolutionStatus option list into a shared `client/src/constants/incidentStatuses.js` so there's one list instead of two (plus the backend's `ALLOWED_STATUSES` as a third, unavoidable copy). Not required, but this is the natural moment.

---

## 3. New "Deep Analytics" subpage

### 3.1 Routing
- `client/src/App.jsx`: import `IncidentAnalytics` and add `<Route path="/incidents/analytics" element={<ProtectedRoute allowedRoles={ACCESS.FM_ONLY}><IncidentAnalytics /></ProtectedRoute>} />` next to the existing `/incidents` route.
- **No entry in `Sidebar.jsx`** — confirmed precedent: `/logistics/gate-verification` is FM-only, registered in `App.jsx`, absent from the sidebar, reached only via a button in `TenantLogistics.jsx`. Same shape here.

### 3.2 New page file `client/src/pages/IncidentAnalytics.jsx`
Fetches `GET /api/incident` once (same auth header pattern as the main dashboard), feeds the raw list into pure aggregation functions, renders 4 panels: KPI row (MTTR tile + Accuracy meter side by side), then the confidence-bucket chart, then the funnel. Includes a "← Back to Incident Dashboard" link/button and its own refresh button. Reuses `Sidebar`, `Dashboard.css` (shell) + a new `IncidentAnalytics.css`.

### 3.3 Pure aggregation module `client/src/utils/incidentAnalytics.js`
Four plain, framework-free functions (mirrors `server/services/dashboardAnalytics.js`'s style, just running client-side): `computeMTTR`, `computeAIAccuracy`, `computeConfidenceBuckets`, `computeResolutionFunnel`. Scoping decisions baked into these functions (call out in code comments, since they're not obvious from field names alone):
- **MTTR**: average `(resolvedAt - createdAt)` over incidents where `resolvedAt` is set, plus a 7-point trend bucketed by **browser-local** calendar day (not the SG-day helpers in `attendanceSummary.js`/`dashboardAnalytics.js` — an accepted simplification for a first-pass KPI sparkline; note in comments that swapping to SG-day precision would mean either exposing `sgDateKey` client-side or moving this aggregation server-side).
- **AI Accuracy**: `% of AI-sourced, terminal-state incidents that are NOT 'False Positive'`. AI-sourced = `source !== 'Manual'` (same definition as the split-bar's combined AI count). Terminal = `resolutionStatus` in `['Cleared', 'False Positive']` — an incident still Active/Investigating hasn't been adjudicated yet, so it's excluded from the denominator.
- **Confidence buckets**: 90–100% / 70–89% / below 70%, restricted to AI-sourced + terminal + non-null `confidence_score` (same "adjudicated only" reasoning as above). Each bucket splits into valid vs. false-positive counts.
- **Resolution funnel**: current counts for the 4 linear stages (Active → Investigating → Escalated to Security → Cleared) plus a separate `falsePositiveCount`, since False Positive is a branch off the funnel, not a 5th sequential stage.

### 3.4 The four visuals — form + color, per the dataviz skill

| Item | Form | Why this form | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. MTTR | **Stat tile**: headline value (auto-compact, e.g. "14m") + small 7-point sparkline underneath | "single current value + maybe a trend" is the textbook stat-tile case, not a full trend-line chart | Sparkline bars in de-emphasis gray, current/last day in accent blue. Single series → no legend box needed (the tile's own label already names it). |
| 2a. AI Accuracy | **Meter** (percentage fill bar), not a donut | Skill explicitly calls out "a single ratio against a limit → meter, not a pie of 2 slices" | Fill tiers by value using the app's existing accent/warning/danger vocabulary: ≥90% blue accent, 70–89% amber, <70% red. Track = a lighter step of the same blue-gray card-border tone. |
| 2b. Confidence buckets vs. outcome | Horizontal **stacked bar per bucket** (part-to-whole) | Skill's "part-to-whole → stacked bar" row; valid/false-positive is a good/bad judgment, so it takes **status** colors, not arbitrary categorical hues | Valid = status-good `#0ca30c`, False Positive = status-critical `#d03b3b` — always paired with a ✓/✕ icon + label, never color alone, per the skill's fixed status-palette rule. |
| 4. Resolution funnel | Horizontal bar per stage, reusing `TopAlertZonesChart`'s exact `.zones-list`/`.zone-bar-track` structure | resolutionStatus here is a literal **ordinal** sequence (the skill's own textbook example for ordinal color is "funnel stage") | One hue (blue), 4 monotone lightness steps in stage order: `#86b6ef` → `#5598e7` → `#2a78d6` → `#1c5cab`. Validated with `--ordinal` against the app's dark surface — passes all 4 checks (monotone L, adjacent ΔL ≥0.06, light-end contrast, single hue). Each stage is directly labeled by name, so no separate legend box is needed. Deliberately different from the existing 4-color status badges (red/amber/yellow/green) elsewhere on the main table — those fail the colorblind check between Investigating/Escalated; this ordinal treatment is the corrected version for this one new chart. `False Positive` renders as a set-apart "aside" row below the 4-stage funnel (not omitted, not folded in as a 5th stage). |

### 3.5 CSS
New `client/src/css/IncidentAnalytics.css`: KPI-row grid (2-up, collapsing to 1 column under ~900px), `.ia-stat-tile` card (same visual language as `.inc-stat-card`: `#1e2539` bg, `#2d364f` border, 12px radius), sparkline bars, meter track/fill, confidence-bucket segments, funnel aside row. All hand-rolled CSS/JSX — **no chart library** is installed in this project (confirmed: `client/package.json` has none) and none should be added; every existing chart on the Operations Dashboard is zero-dependency, and these four should match that convention.

---

## 4. Tests

New test files go under the user's own author folder, matching this repo's per-contributor test convention (confirmed folder name: `Ng Ching Heng, Gladwin`, already used under `flowguard-ai/`):

- **`server/tests/Ng Ching Heng, Gladwin/incident-resolved-at.test.js`** — PATCH route tests: stamps `resolvedAt` on entering Cleared or False Positive; does not re-stamp if already set; clears `resolvedAt` on reopening to a non-terminal status; accepts `'False Positive'` as a valid `resolutionStatus` (200, not a 400); confirms the linked `DetectionAlert.update` is never called with a `status` key when `resolutionStatus === 'False Positive'` (locks in the "intentionally unmapped" decision in 1.3).
- **`client/tests/Ng Ching Heng, Gladwin/incidentAnalytics.test.js`** — pure-function tests for the 4 aggregation functions (fixture arrays in, exact shape out — same style as `server/tests/dashboard-analytics.test.js`): MTTR average + zero-filled 7-day trend, excluding `resolvedAt: null` rows; AI Accuracy percentage and tier at the 90%/70% boundaries; confidence-bucket boundary values (exactly 0.90, exactly 0.70) land correctly, non-terminal/Manual/null-confidence rows excluded; funnel stage counts + separate false-positive count, independent of input order.
- **`client/tests/Ng Ching Heng, Gladwin/IncidentSourceSplitBar.test.jsx`** — mounts the main dashboard (or the extracted split-bar piece) with incidents whose `source` includes `'Browser Webcam'`/`'Uploaded Video'` in addition to the 3 literal values, asserting they land in the Object Detection segment/legend count (regression guard for the under-count bug found in 2.1).
- **`client/tests/Ng Ching Heng, Gladwin/IncidentAnalyticsPage.test.jsx`** — mocks `axios.get('/api/incident')`, renders `<IncidentAnalytics />` in a `MemoryRouter` (same `vi.hoisted` pattern as `DashboardAnalytics.test.jsx`), asserts all 4 panel headings render with fixture-derived numbers in their `aria-label`/sr-only table; empty-incidents fixture renders `—`/0 without crashing; axios rejection shows the unavailable banner.
- **Smoke check**: add `'/incidents/analytics'` to the route list asserted present in `client/tests/public-site-poc.test.jsx`'s existing route-registration check, keeping that test current.

---

## 5. Implementation order

1. Model field + migration SQL, run it locally, spot-check the column exists.
2. `incident.js` route changes (ALLOWED_STATUSES + resolvedAt stamp/clear) — write and pass the server tests immediately; this is the only change with real data-integrity risk.
3. Main dashboard split-bar (Section 2.1-2.4) — self-contained, verifiable without the subpage existing.
4. 'False Positive' status wiring on the main dashboard (2.5) — same file, same pass.
5. `incidentAnalytics.js` pure functions (3.3) + their unit tests — fast to iterate on before any JSX exists.
6. `IncidentAnalytics.jsx` page + 4 sub-components + CSS (3.2/3.4/3.5), wired to the already-tested pure functions.
7. Route registration + "View Deep Analytics →" button (3.1, 2.4).
8. Remaining tests (page render, smoke-check route addition).
9. End-to-end manual pass via the `verify` skill.

## 6. Verification

- Run existing + new test suites (`npm test` in `client/` and `server/`) — all should pass, including the new files in Section 4.
- Use the `verify` skill to run the app locally: log in as FM, create a Manual incident and confirm one exists via an AI path (scan-frame or seeded data), mark one incident `Cleared` and one `False Positive` through the edit modal, confirm the split-bar segments/legend counts update live on the main dashboard, click "View Deep Analytics →", confirm all 4 panels render plausible numbers (not "—" for the ones with data), and confirm a Staff or Tenant login is redirected/blocked from `/incidents/analytics` directly.
- Visual pass: open the new split-bar and the 4 subpage charts and eyeball against the color/mark specs above (segment gaps, rounded-end placement, legend dot shape) — the validator checks color only, not layout, so this step isn't optional.

---

### Critical files
- `server/models/IncidentLog.js`
- `server/routes/incident.js`
- `server/migrations/20260803_add_incident_resolved_at.sql` (new)

### 1.2 Migration — new `server/migrations/20260803_add_incident_resolved_at.sql`
Follow the existing idempotent style (`server/migrations/20260729_sync_missing_columns.sql` is the template): header comment explaining purpose/safety, then
```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE incident_logs ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "resolvedAt" TIMESTAMPTZ;
COMMIT;
```
No backfill — existing Cleared incidents get `resolvedAt = NULL` and simply don't contribute to MTTR until they're touched again. (`updatedAt` was considered and rejected as a backfill proxy: it's bumped by unrelated edits like notes changes, so it would misreport resolution time.) Add a row to `server/migrations/README.md`'s table.

### 1.3 Route — `server/routes/incident.js`
- `ALLOWED_STATUSES` (line 14): append `'False Positive'`.
- `RESOLUTION_TO_ALERT_STATUS` (lines 19-24): **leave unchanged, deliberately**. `DetectionAlert`'s own `VALID_STATUSES` (in `detectionAlerts.js`) has no false-positive analog, so a PATCH that sets `resolutionStatus: 'False Positive'` simply won't touch the linked alert's status — already the route's existing safe no-op path for any unmapped value.
- PATCH `/:id` (lines 210-250): add resolvedAt stamping.
  - Define `const TERMINAL_STATUSES = ['Cleared', 'False Positive'];`
  - When `resolutionStatus` is present in the request: if it's entering a terminal state and `resolvedAt` isn't already set, stamp `resolvedAt = new Date()`. If it's **leaving** a terminal state back to Active/Investigating/Escalated (a reopen) and `resolvedAt` was set, clear it back to `null`. Otherwise leave `resolvedAt` untouched.
  - Reasoning for the clear-on-reopen behavior: MTTR should reflect the incident's *current* resolution cycle, not a stale timestamp from a first resolution that got reopened.

### 1.4 No new backend aggregation endpoint (explicit decision)
`GET /api/incident` already returns every field every chart needs (`source`, `confidence_score`, `resolutionStatus`, `createdAt`, and after 1.1/1.2, `resolvedAt`) for every incident. Compute all four analytics client-side (Section 3.4) rather than adding a `server/services/incidentAnalytics.js` + route — this matches how `stats`/`sourceCounts` are already computed client-side on this exact page today, keeps the subpage's numbers trivially in agreement with the main dashboard (same source list, no separate query to drift), and is easiest to iterate on for an "initial draft." const sourceCounts = useMemo(() => {
  const manual = incidents.filter(i => i.source === 'Manual').length;
  const fr     = incidents.filter(i => i.source === 'Facial Recognition').length;
  const od     = incidents.length - manual - fr; // everything else — see note below
  return { manual, fr, od };

**Important correction found during planning**: `IncidentLog.source` isn't limited to the 3 literal values — `detectionAlerts.js` and `edgeDetectionAlerts.js` also write `'Browser Webcam'`, `'Uploaded Video'`, and `'SecurePi Edge Node'` into real `IncidentLog` rows. ### 3.2 New page file `client/src/pages/IncidentAnalytics.jsx`
Fetches `GET /api/incident` once (same auth header pattern as the main dashboard), feeds the raw list into pure aggregation functions, renders 4 panels: KPI row (MTTR tile + Accuracy meter side by side), then the confidence-bucket chart, then the funnel. Includes a "← Back to Incident Dashboard" link/button and its own refresh button. Reuses `Sidebar`, `Dashboard.css` (shell) + a new `IncidentAnalytics.css`.

### 3.3 Pure aggregation module `client/src/utils/incidentAnalytics.js`
Four plain, framework-free functions (mirrors `server/services/dashboardAnalytics.js`'s style, just running client-side): `computeMTTR`, `computeAIAccuracy`, `computeConfidenceBuckets`, `computeResolutionFunnel`. Scoping decisions baked into these functions (call out in code comments, since they're not obvious from field names alone):
- **MTTR**: average `(resolvedAt - createdAt)` over incidents where `resolvedAt` is set, plus a 7-point trend bucketed by **browser-local** calendar day (not the SG-day helpers in `attendanceSummary.js`/`dashboardAnalytics.js` — an accepted simplification for a first-pass KPI sparkline; note in comments that swapping to SG-day precision would mean either exposing `sgDateKey` client-side or moving this aggregation server-side).
- **AI Accuracy**: `% of AI-sourced, terminal-state incidents that are NOT 'False Positive'`. AI-sourced = `source !== 'Manual'` (same definition as the split-bar's combined AI count). Terminal = `resolutionStatus` in `['Cleared', 'False Positive']` — an incident still Active/Investigating hasn't been adjudicated yet, so it's excluded from the denominator.
- **Confidence buckets**: 90–100% / 70–89% / below 70%, restricted to AI-sourced + terminal + non-null `confidence_score` (same "adjudicated only" reasoning as above). Each bucket splits into valid vs. false-positive counts.
- **Resolution funnel**: current counts for the 4 linear stages (Active → Investigating → Escalated to Security → Cleared) plus a separate `falsePositiveCount`, since False Positive is a branch off the funnel, not a 5th sequential stage.

Resolution funnel | Horizontal bar per stage, reusing `TopAlertZonesChart`'s exact `.zones-list`/`.zone-bar-track` structure | resolutionStatus here is a literal **ordinal** sequence (the skill's own textbook example for ordinal color is "funnel stage") | One hue (blue), 4 monotone lightness steps in stage order: `#86b6ef` → `#5598e7` → `#2a78d6` → `#1c5cab`. # Server migrations

Plain, idempotent SQL migrations for the live PostgreSQL database. The project has
no Sequelize-CLI migration framework, so these are hand-run `.sql` files. Every file
is written to be safe to run more than once (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, no drops).

## Running a migration

From the `server/` directory, using the same credentials as `.env`
(`DB_HOST` / `DB_PORT` / `DB_USER` / `DB_NAME`):

```bash
# PowerShell / Windows (psql from the PostgreSQL install)
$env:PGPASSWORD = "<DB_PWD>"
& "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\18\bin\psql.exe" `
    -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres -d flowguard `
    -f migrations/20260714_sync_object_detection_schema.sql
```

```bash
# bash
PGPASSWORD='<DB_PWD>' psql -h localhost -p 5432 -U postgres -d flowguard \
    -f migrations/20260714_sync_object_detection_schema.sql
```

Each migration wraps its changes in a transaction, so a failure rolls back cleanly
and leaves the database untouched.

## Migrations

| File | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `20260714_sync_object_detection_schema.sql` | Adds the two Object Detection columns that existed in the Sequelize models but not in the live DB after the group-final merge: `monitoring_zones.detection_type` and `detection_alerts.incident_log_id`. Fixes the 500s on `GET /api/zones` and `GET /api/cameras`. |
| `20260729_edge_idempotency_and_whatsapp.sql` | Adds four `detection_alerts` columns for SecurePi edge idempotency + WhatsApp security-alert tracking: `edge_event_id` (unique when non-null — the retry-safe idempotency key), `whatsapp_status` (default `Not Requested`), `whatsapp_sent_at`, `whatsapp_error`. Guarded unique index avoids duplicating Sequelize's own constraint on a fresh DB. |

Base directory for this skill: c:\Fullstack Assignment (FlowGuard)\FlowGuard\.claude\skills\verify

# Verifying FlowGuard changes

## Launch

- Backend: `cd server && npm run dev` (nodemon, listens on **127.0.0.1:5001** via `APP_PORT` in `server/.env`; needs local Postgres running — Sequelize syncs models on boot and prints "FlowGuard Server is FULLY READY").
- Frontend: `cd client && npm run dev` (Vite, default port 5173; picks the next free port if taken — read the actual port from Vite's output). Vite proxies `/api` and `/user` to 5001.

## Auth (bypass login)

Login requires live Google reCAPTCHA, so don't drive the login form. `ProtectedRoute` only checks localStorage, and API middleware (`server/middlewares/auth.js`) only verifies the JWT signature — no DB lookup. Mint a token with the server's own secret:

```bash
cd server && node -e "
require('dotenv').config();
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
console.log(jwt.sign({ id: 1, email: 'admin@harrison.com', role: 'FM' }, process.env.APP_SECRET, { expiresIn: '2h' }));"
```

Then before page load set localStorage: `accessToken` = token, `userRole` = `FM` (or `Staff`/`Tenant`), `userName`, `userId`. Seeded FM account (see `server/seed.js`): admin@harrison.com / Admin123!.

## Drive

No Playwright in the repo; `npm i playwright` in a scratch dir and launch with `channel: 'msedge'` (system Edge — avoids the browser download). Inject localStorage via `context.addInitScript`, then goto e.g. `/incidents`, `/support-dashboard`.

## Gotchas

- Port 5173 is often taken by the user's own running dev server — yours lands on 5174+.
- All page CSS is globally bundled: rules scoped like `.dashboard-main .management-table` leak across pages. Page-specific table rules should use a page-specific class (see `.inc-table`).
- A floating chatbot button + reCAPTCHA badge overlay the bottom-right corner on dashboard pages; they can cover table action buttons in screenshots.

**Built (per the approved plan):**
- Backend: `resolvedAt` column + migration, `'False Positive'` status, PATCH route stamps/clears `resolvedAt` on terminal-state transitions

**Two things worth knowing, unrelated to correctness:**
1. Your local dev DB now has one extra test incident ("PW Verify Loading Bay") and two incidents whose status I changed during verification (one → Cleared, one → False Positive) — harmless for a dev DB, but let me know if you'd like me to revert or delete them.

This machine's Node version (25.8.0) has an experimental built-in `localStorage` that currently breaks the *entire* client test suite (not just mine) unless run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage` — pre-existing, unrelated to this feature, but worth pinning/fixing at the project level if your CI hits the same Node version.

Nothing has been committed — let me know if you'd like me to commit this.

5. Removed the now-dead `.support-tabs`/`.support-tab` CSS rules from `SupportDashboard.css` (both the base and mobile-media-query versions).
6. Updated the route-registration smoke test to include `/knowledge-base`.

Verified: full client suite (69 files / 651 tests) passes, ESLint is clean on all touched/new files, and a live browser walkthrough confirmed the sidebar order, both page headers, the removed tabber, and all navigation paths (sidebar → Incidents & Support, sidebar → Knowledge Base, Incident Dashboard button → Support Tickets) work with zero console errors.
